states.name: q
states.meaning: 16-bit four-digit BCD counter state: q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands; each digit is 0 through 9.

rules.condition: reset == 1; at the posedge clk, q becomes 16'h0000.

reset == 0; at each posedge clk q becomes the 4-digit BCD increment of its previous value: ones increments 0..9 then wraps to 0 and carries to tens, hundreds, and thousands; 9999 wraps to 0000. The example begins from the documented post-reset state q=0.

Combinational from settled q: ena[0] = (q[3:0] == 9) for tens increment; ena[1] = (q[3:0] == 9 && q[7:4] == 9) for hundreds increment; ena[2] = (q[3:0] == 9 && q[7:4] == 9 && q[11:8] == 9) for thousands increment.
rules.spec_quote: For digits [3:1], also output an enable signal indicating when each of the upper three digits should be incremented.

reset.name: reset
reset.first_released_cycle: The first sampled posedge with reset=0 after reset; on that edge q updates by the BCD increment rule and ena reflects the resulting q.

mid: Optional mid input changes occur after a sampled posedge and before the next negedge; they are carried to the start of the next row. No mid changes are used in the examples.

uncertain.note: The reset value is not explicitly stated in the public spec; q=0 and ena=0 are assumed for a BCD counter reset.
candidates: reset value is unspecified; q and ena may take an implementation-defined value
